February, 2025

Author: Vivek Rusia
Bench: Vivek Rusia
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
 Cra No. 6587 of 2022
 (Reva Prasad Tiwar Vs The State Of Madhaya Pradesh 
 Dated : 10-02-2025
 Shri Devendra Singh - Advocate for the appellant.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Akhilendra Singh - G.A. for respondent/State.

Heard on I.A. No.13913 of 2024 which is second application under Section 389(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant.

His first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 25.04.2023.
2.

The trial Court has convicted the appellant under Section 323, 376 and 506 Part II of IPC and Section 3(2)(5) of SC/ST Act and sentenced him to undergo 1 year R.I. with fine of Rs. 500/-, 10 years R.I. with fine of Rs. 3,000/-, 3 Years R.I. with fine of Rs. 1,000/- and Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs. 10,000/- and default stipulations.
3. As per prosecution story, the prosecutrix hired the auto rickshaw of the present appellant and after boarding down the other passengers, he took her to the jungle where he committed rape upon her.
Thereafter, she came back in the same auto to her house and then went to the house of the appellant and mother of the prosecutrix followed her.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.
He further submits that there is a delay of two years in lodging the F.I.R..
The prosecutrix is a married lady and she is aged about 40 years.
As per doctor's opinion, no injury was found and there was no forceful sign of rape.
Therefore, in 2 CRA-6587-2022 such circumstances counsel for the appellant submits that she was a consenting party.
Appellant is in jail since 24.01.2021.

This appeal is of the year 2022 and is not likely to be heard finally in near future and it would take sufficient long time, therefore, prays for suspension of jail sentence of appellant and to release him on bail.
5.
Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State opposes the aforesaid application and prays for its rejection.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.
6. In view of the above facts and circumstances of the case in totality, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
7. Accordingly I.A. No.13913 of 2024 is allowed.

It is directed that the jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail upon his depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) and also upon furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 10.07.2025 and on such further dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the concerned trial Court during the pendency of this appeal.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
(VIVEK RUSIA)
(ANURA  JUDGE
